description: A four-panel composite of SEM micrographs comparing Nb-containing medium-Mn low-density steels aged at 723 K. Every panel carries a 20 µm scale bar (bottom right) and a temperature/time label in the top-right: (a) and (c) read "723 K/6 h", (b) and (d) read "723 K/9 h". Each shows a two-phase microstructure: a light grey matrix with darker, irregular elongated and script-like features. Yellow arrows are labelled δ (delta ferrite) pointing at the dark phase; a yellow "γ" marks the austenite matrix. Purple arrows point to small bright particles (NbC precipitates) scattered through the matrix. The caption assigns (a),(b) to the 0.02Nb steel and (c),(d) to the 0.04Nb steel, so the panels compare 6 h versus 9 h ageing for each composition. Across the panels the δ-phase boundaries look progressively more irregular and bulging with prolonged ageing, and the bright precipitates coarsen, most noticeably in the 0.04Nb panels (c) and (d). The figure demonstrates that prolonged 723 K ageing roughens the ferrite/austenite interfaces and grows NbC particles without evident change in phase fractions.

observations.observation: All four panels are SEM micrographs with a 20 µm scale bar.
Panel (a) is labelled "723 K/6 h"; panel (b) is labelled "723 K/9 h".
Panel (c) is labelled "723 K/6 h"; panel (d) is labelled "723 K/9 h".
Yellow arrows labelled δ mark the darker phase and a yellow γ label marks the matrix in every panel.
Purple arrows point to small bright particles within the matrix in all four panels.
The caption states (a),(b) are SEM images of the 0.02Nb steel and (c),(d) of the 0.04Nb steel, aged at 723 K for different periods.
The citing text reports ferrite contents of 17.1 and 18.9 vol% for the 0.02Nb steel aged at 723 K for 6 and 9 h.
The citing text reports ferrite contents of 17.5 and 18.8 vol% for the 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K for 6 and 9 h.

The citing text states the phase boundaries between ferrite and austenite become irregular with numerous bulges as ageing time prolongs, but the volume fraction of phases does not change significantly.
The citing text states that the NbC particle size in the 0.04Nb steel increases significantly with prolonged ageing compared to the 0.02Nb steel.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph labelled "723 K/6 h", 20 µm scale bar. Light grey austenite matrix with darker irregular δ-phase regions pointed to by yellow arrows; yellow "γ" label; purple arrows mark small bright NbC-type particles. Assigned by the caption to the 0.02Nb steel.

SEM micrograph labelled "723 K/9 h", 20 µm scale bar. Similar two-phase structure with darker δ regions marked by yellow arrows and yellow "γ"; purple arrows point to bright particles. Assigned by the caption to the 0.02Nb steel.
SEM micrograph labelled "723 K/6 h", 20 µm scale bar. Darker δ regions with yellow arrows and yellow "γ" label; purple arrows indicate bright particles. Assigned by the caption to the 0.04Nb steel.

SEM micrograph labelled "723 K/9 h", 20 µm scale bar. Darker irregular δ regions marked by yellow arrows, yellow "γ" label, purple arrows marking bright particles. Assigned by the caption to the 0.04Nb steel.

unreadable_items: No quantitative particle-size or phase-fraction values are printed on the images; the vol% and NbC-size figures come only from the citing text.
The individual particles marked by purple arrows are too small to resolve for size measurement at the supplied resolution.
